text:
emily: idea: add a visible "risk budget" burn-bar next to the fallback controls. shows remaining allowed degraded requests in the window.

karl: love that. operators always ask "how long till we exhaust fallback budget?" This answers it.

vishal: implementation thought: budget = configurable % of requests or absolute count per-route per-window. show both.

anita: UX: the bar should have three states: healthy (green), caution (amber), panic (red). when in panic, auto-throttle fallback rate down and surface an alert.

emily: auto-throttle = "panic throttle"? meaning we reduce aggressiveness automatically when budget burn > threshold. that could prevent runaway costs.

karl: yes, but panic throttle must be auditable and reversible. log event with audit_id and reason.

guard-bot: guard-bot: note: any automatic change must be tagged as automated_action=true in audit log.

vishal: breadcrumb shape for these events: compact tuple like `{"r":"budget_burn","b":0.87,"action":"throttle","aid":"pb7"}` aim ~150B.
anita: show a small "why" popover on each breadcrumb: one-liner explanation and link to full trace if available. avoid heavy traces on hot paths.

emily: preview/what-if: allow operator to run a "burn-forward" sim which shows how long the budget lasts at current traffic and aggressiveness. non-invasive, sim=true.
karl: show two numbers: projected time to exhaustion and expected mean degraded-rate while throttle active. both derived from sampled telemetry.
vishal: storage policy: breadcrumbs 365d, auto-action traces 90d, full decision traces 30d. orgs can override. automated_action traces are slightly larger by design.
anita: microcopy draft: "Risk budget limits how many requests can be routed to fallback modes in a rolling window. Panic throttle temporarily reduces fallback aggressiveness when the budget is nearly exhausted to protect cost/slas."

emily: per-route and org-level budgets. per-route defaults inherit org budget split but operators can set route caps. show small inline formula: "route cap = org_budget * route_share" and a link to docs.

karl: RBAC: only platform-admins can change budgets and disable panic throttle. on-call can acknowledge and temporarily increase budget with one-click (and an audit checkbox requiring reason).

ops-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary for burnbar + panic-throttle on staging at 01:30 UTC :rocket:

vishal: telemetry tagging: when panic throttle activates, emit a compact audit breadcrumb and a sampled full trace for the event (sample 1%) to help postmortem. link via aid.

anita: add a UI timeline under the burn-bar that shows recent actions (auto-throttle events, manual overrides) with timestamps and links. useful during incident.

emily: UX nicety: let operators click the burn-bar to open a tiny simulator modal where they can nudge aggressiveness and see instant projected burn time. changes are simulated unless they click "Apply".
karl: safety: when Apply used in prod, require justification text + optional ticket link; record in audit log.
vishal: breadcrumb example for manual override: `{"r":"manual_override","by":"karl","delta":0.2,"aid":"m9q"}`. keep keys short.

anita: retention/PII: ensure manual notes are scrubbed for PII in exports. add export flag.

guard-bot: guard-bot: compliance rule recorded: manual_override notes are redacted in compliance export unless explicit opt-in by compliance admins.

emily: action items: 1) @vishal draft breadcrumb + audit_id schema and ingestion compatibility notes. 2) @karl mock burn-bar + simulator modal (Figma). 3) @anita write RBAC & compliance flows. 4) I'll draft the product spec and example microcopy.
vishal: I'll include storage estimates for 200B crumbs at projected 3k QPS and additional cost for sampled traces.
karl: I'll add a small storyboard showing panic throttle behaviour during a spike.
anita: I'll draft the confirmation modal text and the export redaction rules.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary scheduled; will tag preview events with sim=true and auto-action events with automated_action=true :gear:

emily: ok team, if staging sim looks sane we can propose defaults next platform sync. thanks all :thumbsup:
